title: URL Shortener
summary: A read-heavy key-value lookup: generate collision-free short codes, serve redirects from cache in under 10 ms, and count clicks asynchronously.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Create a short URL from a long URL; optional custom alias and expiry
Click analytics per link (count, country, referrer, time)
Redirect p99 < 50 ms globally; 99.99% availability on the redirect path
Codes never collide and are not trivially guessable

items: Out of scope: user accounts UI, link-in-bio pages, malware scanning (mention as follow-up).

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: It's 100:1 read-heavy, so the redirect path lives in cache. 1,200 writes per second is modest; the hard parts are unique code generation and serving 350k redirects a second at the edge.

head: Table
Key
Fields
Store
rows: DynamoDB / Cassandra (KV, horizontally partitioned by code)

blocks.text: The only hot query is `code → long_url`, a single-key lookup with no joins, so a partitioned KV store fits. Sharding by code spreads load evenly because codes are effectively random.

blocks.caption: Redirect path served from edge and cache; writes go through ID allocation

items: **Write:** create service takes the next ID from its locally held range, base62-encodes it, writes `code → url` to the KV store, returns the short URL.
**Read:** CDN miss → redirect service checks Redis → on miss reads KV, fills Redis (TTL 24 h) → returns 302 and emits a click event to Kafka without waiting.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Sequential IDs make codes guessable. Pass the ID through a reversible permutation (e.g. multiply by a large odd number mod 62^7, or a Feistel cipher) before encoding.
Custom aliases are inserted with a conditional write (`attribute_not_exists(code)`) so two users can't claim the same alias.

cols.title: 301 Moved Permanently
cons: Later clicks bypass you → analytics lost

cols.title: 302 Found
pros: Every click reaches you → full analytics

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd return 302 so we keep analytics and can expire links, and get the speed back with a short edge cache (30–60 s) plus Redis. The hot set is small: the top 20% of codes serve about 80% of clicks.
Cache sizing: 115k reads/s, ~20% of daily distinct codes are hot. If 1B distinct codes are hit per day, 200M × 500 B ≈ 100 GB of Redis across a cluster.

items: Redirect never waits on analytics: publish `{code, ts, ip, ua, referrer}` to Kafka and return.
Stream processor (Flink) enriches with geo-IP, aggregates per code per minute, writes to ClickHouse.
Exact per-click rows go to cheap object storage for reprocessing.
Dashboards read pre-aggregated rollups; counts are eventually consistent (seconds).

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: Counting with `UPDATE urls SET clicks = clicks + 1` on every redirect turns a read path into a hot-row write path. Never do this.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Replicas + client-side retry on replica; KV autoscaling; request coalescing
Edge cache + in-process LRU on redirect servers
Servers hold a buffer of 2 ranges; allocator runs as leader with standby (etcd lease)
Rate limit creates per user/IP, Safe Browsing check async, takedown flag
Multi-region active-active reads; KV global tables; GeoDNS failover

items.title: Requirements
items.text: Create, redirect, analytics, expiry, custom alias. Confirm 100:1 read-heavy.

items.title: Non-functional
items.text: p99 < 50 ms redirects, 99.99% available, no collisions.

items.title: Estimation
items.text: 1.2k writes/s, 115k reads/s, 7-char base62, ~90 TB over 5 years.

items.title: API + data
items.text: POST /urls, GET /{code}; KV table keyed by code.

items.title: HLD
items.text: CDN → redirect svc → Redis → KV; create svc with range allocator; Kafka for clicks.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Code generation options, 301 vs 302 + caching, analytics pipeline.

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Hot keys, abuse, multi-region, monitoring redirect p99 and cache hit rate.

items.q: How do you handle the same long URL submitted twice?
items.a: Either allow duplicates (simplest, per-user links have different analytics) or keep a secondary index `hash(longUrl, owner) → code` and return the existing code.

items.q: How do expired links get cleaned up?
items.a: Store `expires_at`; the redirect path checks it (410 Gone). A TTL attribute in DynamoDB/Cassandra deletes rows lazily; invalidate the cache key on expiry.

items.q: Why not use a SQL database?
items.a: One would work up to a point with sharding, but there are no joins or transactions; a KV store gives simpler horizontal scaling for 180B rows.

items.q: How would you make codes unpredictable?
items.a: Permute the counter value with a keyed bijection before base62, or use random codes with conditional writes and retry.
Redirect p50/p99, cache hit ratio (target > 95%), 4xx/5xx rate, allocator range remaining, Kafka consumer lag.

items.q: How do you prevent enumeration scraping?
items.a: Rate limit by IP at the edge, non-sequential codes, bot detection on high 404 rates.

items: 100:1 reads → cache + CDN dominate the design.
Range allocation: unique codes, one coordination call per block.
302 keeps analytics; 301 is faster but blind.
Clicks go async through Kafka into a columnar store.
Shard KV by code; it's random so load is even.
Hot links: edge cache + local LRU.
Never increment a counter on the redirect row.
